title: trailboss --json branch
description: One row: the fork of a session `branch` would start (no --yes), or started (--yes), to ask a side question: the agent's own fork of that session, in a new host terminal in the session's folder (or, with --worktree, in a new git worktree of its repository on a new branch `branch/<n>-<slug>`, kept as a task so `task ls`, `task show`, `task accept` and `task rm` work on it), leaving the session itself alone. The command runs directly, never through a shell. Started, it's kept as started from the session, so `live`, `resume`, `sweep` and `thread --tree` show it there. An agent whose CLI has no fork, a session that isn't indexed or whose folder is gone, and a start that fails are errors, not rows. Frontends should show an action they don't know as is.

action.description: would branch or branched; more may be added.

parent.description: AGENT:ID of the session branched from.

kind.description: The agent: claude for now; more as their CLIs offer a fork.

at.description: --at: the turn (as `thread` numbers them) whose prompt the first prompt quotes, everything after it set aside; null to branch from the session's end.

folder.description: The folder it runs in: the session's, or with --worktree the new worktree.

argv.description: What it runs, with the question shown as `<question>`. With --at, the first prompt also holds a fixed sentence quoting the first line of your prompt at that turn. Without a question, no first prompt: it waits for you.

command.description: argv as one line to read; nothing runs it through a shell.

question.description: Whether it was given a question (--prompt or --prompt-file). The question itself isn't printed.

label.description: --name, else `KIND branch`: its terminal's name, and what `live` and `resume` show.

host.description: herdr, tmux, …; null when no host is running (the plan then says so).

terminal.description: The new terminal's address, once started.

task.description: With --worktree: the task number it's kept as (the next one, in a plan); else null.

worktree.description: With --worktree: the new worktree's folder; else null.

branch.description: With --worktree: the new git branch, `branch/<n>-<slug>`; else null.

base.description: With --worktree: the branch checked out in the session's folder, which `task accept` fast-forwards to the new branch; else null.

start.description: With --worktree: where the new branch starts. `commit` is the commit; `checkpoint` the session's checkpoint number whose files are written into the worktree, uncommitted (the first one saved after `turn` ended and before the next turn began), or null when none was, and the branch starts from the folder's HEAD; `turn` is --at, else the session's last turn, null with none. Else null.

ignore.description: With --worktree, when the worktrees folder is inside the repository and git doesn't ignore it: the line that ignores it (as `task add`'s). Else null.

mid_edit.description: Tracked files with uncommitted changes in the session's folder; null when it isn't in a git repository. Without --worktree, more than 0 makes the plan suggest --worktree.
